why: Sleep, food, and hydration provide resources for energy, adaptation, and participation in recovery.

slides.title: Recovery Takes Resources
slides.content: Your body is always adapting. Sleep, regular nourishment, and hydration help support energy, tissue processes, concentration, mood, and your ability to participate in movement and daily life.

slides.title: Sleep Supports the System
slides.content: Sleep can influence pain sensitivity, energy, mood, learning, and recovery behaviours. One difficult night does not erase progress, and trying to force perfect sleep can create more pressure.

slides.title: Food Supports the Work
slides.content: Regular, balanced eating helps provide energy and nutrients for everyday function and recovery. No single food fixes pain, and eating does not need to be perfect to be useful.

slides.title: Hydration Is a Foundation
slides.content: Hydration supports normal body function and activity. Needs vary with the person, health, activity, and environment; more water is not automatically better.

slides.title: Support—Not Blame
slides.content: Poor sleep, irregular meals, or low fluid intake do not prove why you hurt. They are modifiable supports that may make recovery and participation easier when they need attention.

slides.title: Choose One Anchor
slides.content: Pick one realistic action: a consistent wake time, one reliable meal, or a drink paired with a regular routine. Keep moving and following your care plan while you test it.
